checks: Classic (EndTxn v4) and transaction-V2 (EndTxn v5) identity handling: classic abort re-inits with the last broker-authorized (pid, epoch) via InitProducerId; V2 applies the EndTxn-response identity with no re-init (init count stays 1); fencing never invents an identity (epoch unchanged, init count 1, no EndTxn sent)

Abort-required vs fatal: UNKNOWN_PRODUCER_ID (produce and EndTxn), GROUP_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED (TxnOffsetCommit/AddOffsets) are abort-required and sticky until abort; PRODUCER_FENCED, INVALID_PRODUCER_ID_MAPPING, TRANSACTIONAL_ID_AUTHORIZATION_FAILED (produce, EndTxn, AddPartitions, AddOffsets, TxnOffsetCommit) are fatal and terminal; unit matrix in protocol::txn pins all six Java handler tables

Replacement transactional producer: second producer with the same transactional.id gets the same pid with a bumped epoch from the broker; the stale producer is fenced on its next produce (no forced errors) while the replacement commits records plus offsets

Outputs and consumed offsets share one outcome: TxnOffsetCommit stages in the broker until EndTxn; commit applies both, abort discards both; lost-commit retry stays idempotent (single committed outcome) and abort-after-ambiguous-commit leaves nothing committed; offsets outside an open transaction are rejected with no RPC

Ambiguous EndTxn sets no sticky state: transport Timeout/Io during EndTxn leaves the transaction open for a safe idempotent retry or abort; a broker-side close no longer bricks the coordinator channel (Closed now rediscovers like other transport failures)
External-side-effect limits documented on begin/commit/abort: EOS covers broker records plus offsets only; side effects must happen after commit and tolerate duplicates on ambiguous outcomes
